title: An independent plan checker

blocks.text: A telecom operator wants every plan its optimizer returns checked by code that shares nothing with the model: it reads only the data and the plan. Write `broken_rules(plan, projects, limits)` in `checker.py`. `plan` is the set of funded project ids. It returns the sorted list of labels of every rule the plan breaks, and an empty list when it breaks none:

items: `"budget"`: the plan's total cost is above `limits.budget`;
`"region_<r>"`: more projects in region `r` than `limits.region_cap[r]`; a region with no entry in `limits.region_cap` has no cap, however many of its projects are funded;
`"conflict_<a>_<b>"`: both projects of a pair in `limits.conflicts` are funded;
`"needs_<a>_<b>"`: for a pair `(a, b)` in `limits.needs`, `a` is funded without `b`.

blocks.text: Report every broken rule, not only the first. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
from checker import Limits, Project, broken_rules

piers = [
    Project("P1", 50, 2, "East"),
    Project("P2", 35, 3, "East"),
    Project("P3", 25, 2, "West"),
    Project("P4", 40, 4, "West"),
    Project("P5", 15, 1, "North"),
]
limits = Limits(budget=110, crew=8, region_cap={"East": 1, "West": 2, "North": 1},
                conflicts=[("P1", "P4")], needs=[("P5", "P3")])

for plan in ({"P1", "P3", "P5"}, {"P1", "P2"}, {"P1", "P4"}, {"P5"}, {"P1", "P2", "P3", "P4"}):
    print(f"plan {sorted(plan)}:", broken_rules(plan, piers, limits))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    cost: int            # $k
    crew: int            # crew-weeks
    region: str
    value: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Limits:
    budget: int
    crew: int
    region_cap: dict[str, int]
    conflicts: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)   # not both
    needs: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)       # (a, b): a only if b


def broken_rules(plan: set[str], projects: list[Project], limits: Limits) -> list[str]:
    """Every rule the plan breaks, read from the data alone, as sorted labels."""
    # TODO: check each rule against the plan, using only the data.
    return ["unchecked"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    projects = [Project("A", 40, 3, "N"), Project("B", 30, 2, "N")]
    print(broken_rules({"A", "B"}, projects, Limits(60, 4, {"N": 1})))

cases.says: a plan within every rule breaks nothing, and one over the budget breaks the budget
a plan with both projects of a conflicting pair breaks that conflict
a project that is needed may be funded alone, and one that needs it may not
a region with exactly its cap of projects breaks nothing
a plan that breaks several rules reports all of them
a region missing from the caps has no cap, and a region with a cap still has one
